claims.text: Rapid quenching or similarly fast cooling produces HfNbTaTiZr with a random, chemically disordered elemental distribution and minimal short-range order.
Controlled exposure between 800°C and 1200°C permits sufficient atomic diffusion in HfNbTaTiZr for short-range chemical order to develop.
The 800–1200°C range is below the melting and phase-decomposition limits of the relevant HfNbTaTiZr state.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr forms localized clusters that change the local lattice environment and bonding.
Elevated temperature enables selective, diffusion-controlled atomic rearrangement that generates short-range order.
Short-range ordering reduces the variability of local interatomic spacing in HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced interatomic-spacing variability lowers the thermal expansion coefficient.
Short-range ordering stiffens the HfNbTaTiZr lattice and increases its elastic modulus.
Short-range ordering impedes dislocation motion in HfNbTaTiZr.
The impediment of dislocation motion modifies yield and plastic-deformation behavior in stress–strain curves.
SRO-promoting thermal treatment will lower the thermal expansion coefficient relative to rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr between 800°C and 1200°C.
SRO-promoting thermal treatment will increase the elastic modulus relative to rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr between 800°C and 1200°C.
SRO-promoting thermal treatment will increase yield strength relative to rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr between 800°C and 1200°C.
SRO-promoting thermal treatment will alter strain-hardening behavior relative to rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr between 800°C and 1200°C.
Below the proposed temperature range, diffusion is too slow for the hypothesized short-range ordering response.
Above the proposed range, melting or other phase changes invalidate the hypothesized response.
